terms.grammar: conjunction, with the indicative; often answered by ita or sīc
evidence: Ter. And. 310: Age age, ut libet.
terms.comment: The plain “as”, in comparisons and in asides: ut ajunt, as they say; ut soleō, as usual; ut libet, as you like.

terms.grammar: conjunction, with the indicative; answered by ita or sīc
relative adverb, with the indicative; answered by sīc or ita
evidence: Sen. Ep. 47.11: sīc cum īnferiōre vīvās quemadmodum tēcum superiōrem velīs vīvere
terms.comment: “In what way”: also the question “how?” and, in an indirect question, with the subjunctive (quaeris quemadmodum … diem dispōnam, Plin. Ep. 9.36.1).

phrases.english: keep on as you have begun
All right, all right, as you like.
as they say, the gods help those who get on with it

phrases.latin: S. V. B. E. V., sīcut soleō, paululō tamen etiam dēterius quam soleō
phrases.english: if you are well, good; I am well, as usual, though a little worse even than usual

phrases.latin: sīc cum īnferiōre vīvās quemadmodum tēcum superiōrem velīs vīvere
phrases.english: live with those below you as you would want those above you to live with you
